verdict.line: You lose if you keep eating shielded W poke through an open wave and let him control range to 6; you win if you deny his cooldown windows and force free melee trades where your bleed and grievous wounds close him out.

brief.thesis: This is a genuinely even lane (50% Darius overall, 51.3% over 731 games vs Mordekaiser) because both champions win the fight a different way: Morde wants to chip you down from range with W (Siphon of Destruction) and bank a shield off Darkness Rise before he ever enters your E (Apprehend) range, while Darius wants to force the melee exchange where his passive bleed and W (Crippling Strike) healing cut outpace Morde's frontloaded magic burst. Whoever dictates when the fight actually starts wins it.

theirWindow.when: his shield is freshly up from a landed spell
theirWindow.what: He's confident to all-in with the extra effective HP from Darkness Rise. Back off and let it decay (a few seconds without him landing another ability) instead of trading into a shielded Morde.

yourWindow.when: his E (Death's Grasp) and Q (Obliterate) are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: He has no gap-close and no delayed burst queued. Hook him with E (Apprehend), lay W (Crippling Strike) for the healing cut, and dump Q (Decimate) — he can't escape or out-trade you in straight melee.

start.why: Best-performing start at 52.3% over 751 games and by far the most picked (79.6%) — the extra sustain and auto damage matter more here than Doran's Shield's flat mitigation since most of Morde's early damage lands as burst spell hits, not chip autos.

boots.why: Highest-picked boots (67.3%) at 50.2% wr, and correct into Mordekaiser specifically — Q, W, E, and R all deal magic damage, so the flat MR directly reduces every source of his damage, unlike Plated Steelcaps which answers physical poke he doesn't have.

core.why: Best-performing core path starts here (68.4% wr over 38 games) — the active gives you the burst of movement speed to close from outside his W range and the haste to chain E into full combo before his shield resets.
Second item on the top-performing path; the magic resist directly counters a 100%-magic-damage kit and the movespeed proc helps you stay on top of a champion with no dash of his own.
Rounds out the highest-winrate path — bonus health and the charge-up movespeed let you actually catch him if he tries to kite behind minions before your Ghostblade cooldown is back.

situational.when: he's ahead and you need to survive his burst window to get your own combo off
you're already winning and want to end fights before his shield or Realm of Death changes the outcome
he's built into a tanky AP/HP hybrid and you need the shield plus tenacity to finish him

runes.keystoneWhy: This is the higher-performing page (54% wr, 27.7% pick) and the stacking adaptive damage plus healing rewards exactly the extended melee trades you're trying to force — it converts a won trade into sustain that outlasts his burst.

summoners.why: Highest pick rate by far (64.9%) at 52.4% wr — Ghost is what actually lets you close on a champion with zero dashes once his E speed boost or a minion wave puts distance between you, which matters more here than Ignite's kill pressure since neither side has a reliable early kill window.

playing.title: Hook overextensions level 1-2
playing.detail: Morde has no escape and E (Apprehend) outranges his stubby auto attack. If he pushes past the wave to land W, punish it immediately before his kit comes online.

playing.title: Trade behind minions, not in the open
playing.detail: Position so enemy minions sit between you and his cone so W (Siphon of Destruction) either whiffs or eats reduced damage from hitting minions first. Only step up to trade once the wave has crashed close to you.

playing.title: Let his shield decay before you commit
playing.detail: Darkness Rise only shields him for a few seconds after landing a spell. If you see it pop, disengage and wait it out rather than trading into free effective HP.

playing.title: Lead trades with W for the healing cut
playing.detail: Crippling Strike's grievous wounds blunts the sustain he gets back off Darkness Rise's on-hit heal, so land it before you commit your full combo, not after.

playing.title: Track Death's Grasp before all-inning
playing.detail: E is his only way to speed toward you after a hit. If it's down, he can't chase a disengage or close a gap — this is your green light to E-hook and dump everything.

playing.title: Respect Realm of Death at 6
playing.detail: If he ults you, you're isolated together until it ends — commit your full burst including R (Noxian Guillotine) immediately rather than trying to disengage, since no help is reaching either of you.

playing.title: Rush Force of Nature before he three-items
playing.detail: His entire kit is magic damage, so the MR on your core path pays off every single trade — don't delay it for damage items if he's ahead on gold.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, pick rates, sample sizes, build paths, runes, boots, starting items, and summoner spells above are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch. The mechanical reasoning — why each window opens, how the shield and poke interact, when to commit — is my own tactical read, not part of the measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of being nuked by Mordekaiser’s abilities. Try to fight him when the opponent steps in your range to nuke him in one burst.
